source_text: Καὶ σφόδρα μὲν ἐκπλήττομαι θαυμαστῶς τὴν τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν οἰκονομίαν, ὃς εὐδόκησε τῇ ὑπερβολῇ τῆς αὐτοῦ ἀγαθότητος ἐν ἅπασι δοῦναι τὸ ἅγιον αὐτοῦ Πνεῦμα τοῖς αὐτὸν ἐν ἀληθείᾳ ζητοῦσιν. Οὐκ ἀθέους γὰρ ὑμῶν καὶ τῶν καθ᾽ ὑμᾶς αἰτήσεις τὰς διὰ τῶν γραμμάτων ἡγησάμην, ποθεινότατοι, ἀλλὰ τὴν κίνησιν ἐδοκίμασα ἐκ τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ χάριτος ἐν ὑμῖν ὑπάρξασαν. Ἐπ᾽ ἀληθείας γὰρ, καὶ εἰδότες συνοίδατε, καὶ σύμφωνα λέγειν τῷ μακαριωτάτῳ Πέτρῳ, ὅτι Σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος, σαφῶς ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου μακαρισθήσονται, καθὼς καὶ ὁ ἅγιος ἐκεῖνος ἐμακαρίσθη ἀκούων· Μακάριος εἶ σὺ, Σίμων βὰρ Ἰωνᾶ, τουτέστιν, υἱὲ Ἰωνᾶ (ὁ γὰρ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ Ἰωνᾶς ἐκαλεῖτο· τὸ δὲ βὰρ ἑρμηνεύεται ἐκ τῆς Ἑβραϊκῆς διαλέκτου, υἱός). Καὶ τοῦτο ἦν ἡ ζωή, ἣν ἔδωκεν ὁ μονογενὴς Υἱὸς τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ μαθηταῖς λέγων· Ἵνα ἔχωσι τὴν ζωὴν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, τὸ γινώσκειν τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν Θεὸν, καὶ ὃν ἀπέστειλεν Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν. Ἐν τῷ οὖν εἰπεῖν, Τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν Θεὸν, εἰς μοναρχίαν ἡμᾶς ἤγαγεν· ἵνα μηκέτι ὑπὸ τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου ὦμεν δεδουλωμένοι, ἵνα μὴ πολυθεΐα ἐν ἡμῖν ἔτι ᾖ, καὶ ἐπὶ πορνείαν τοιαύτην ἐπισκορπίζηται τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων νοήματα, ἀλλ᾽ ἐπὶ ἑνότητα τοῦ μόνου ἀληθινοῦ Θεοῦ· Πρώτη γὰρ πορνεία, ἐπίνοια εἰδώλων, φησὶν ἡ Γραφή. Καὶ ὃν ἀπέστειλας Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν. Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τίνα; ἀληθινὸν Θεόν. Εἰ δὲ Θεὸν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν, ὡς λέγει περὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰωάννης· Ὁ Μονογενὴς, ὁ ὢν εἰς τὸν κόλπον τοῦ Πατρὸς, αὐτὸς ἐξηγήσατο· εἷς Θεὸς τοίνυν ὁ Πατήρ, καὶ μόνος ἀληθινὸς Θεός, καὶ οὐ κατὰ τοὺς ἐψευσμένους θεοὺς, οὓς ἐνόμισάν τινες τῶν Ἑλλήνων θεοὺς, οὐκ ὄντας θεούς· ἀλλὰ μόνος ἀληθινὸς Θεός, ἐπειδὴ μόνος ἐκ μόνου ὁ Μονογενής, καὶ μόνον τὸ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα. Τριὰς γὰρ ἐν μονάδι, καὶ εἷς Θεός, Πατὴρ, Υἱὸς καὶ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα.
thought_title: The one true God and the only Son
orientation: Epiphanius is writing to the clergy of Syedra, praising their request and explaining that knowledge of the one true God leads to unity, not polytheism.

Not godless for of you and of those with you the requests the through the letters I considered, most desired [ones], but the movement I tested from the of God grace in you having arisen. In truth for, also knowing you know with [me], also in agreement to say with the most blessed Peter, that You are the Christ the Son of the God of the living, clearly by him the Lord they will be blessed, just as also the holy that [one] was blessed hearing: Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah, that is, son of Jonah (the for father of him Jonah was called; the and bar is interpreted from the Hebrew dialect, son). And this was the life, which gave the only Son to his own disciples saying: That they may have the life in themselves, the to know the only true God, and whom he sent Jesus Christ. In the therefore to say, The only true God, to one rule us he led; that no longer under the elements of the world we may be enslaved, that not polytheism in us still may be, and to fornication such may be scattered the of men thoughts, but to unity of the only true God; First for fornication, invention of idols, says the Scripture. And if God Christ Jesus, as says about him the John: The only Son, the [one] being in the bosom of the Father, that [one] has explained; one God therefore the Father, and only true God, and not according to the false gods, whom considered some of the Greeks gods, not being gods; but only true God, since only from only the only Son, and only the holy Spirit. bible_refs.note: Peter's confession 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God' and Jesus' blessing 'Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah' are paraphrased and quoted.

The words 'that they may have life in themselves, to know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent' adapt John 17:3, changing 'eternal life' to 'life in themselves' and 'you sent' to 'he sent'.
The words 'The only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has made him known' quote John 1:18.
The words 'The invention of idols is the first fornication' quote Wisdom 14:12.

pass_b_english: I am truly astonished, and with good reason, at the plan of our Lord and God. In the overflowing abundance of his goodness, he was pleased to give his Holy Spirit to all who seek him in truth. My dear friends, I did not regard the requests you and those with you sent in your letters as godless. Instead, I tested the impulse behind them and found that it came from the grace of God at work in you.

For in truth, you know and agree together that those who speak in harmony with the most blessed Peter—saying, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God"—will clearly be blessed by the Lord himself, just as that holy man was blessed when he heard, "Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah," that is, son of Jonah. His father was called Jonah, and the word bar is translated from the Hebrew language as "son."

And this was the life that the only Son gave to his own disciples when he said that they might have life in themselves, to know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent (John 17:3). So by saying "the only true God," he led us to the one rule of God, so that we would no longer be enslaved under the elements of the world, so that polytheism would no longer be in us and human thoughts would no longer be scattered toward such fornication, but toward the unity of the only true God. For Scripture says, "The invention of idols is the first fornication" (Wisdom of Solomon 14:12).

And "Jesus Christ whom he sent"—who is this Jesus Christ? He is true God. And if Christ Jesus is God, as John says about him, "The only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has made him known" (John 1:18), then the Father is one God, and he alone is true God—not according to the false gods whom some of the Greeks supposed to be gods, though they are not gods. Rather, he alone is true God, because the only Son is only from the only Father, and the Holy Spirit is only. For the Trinity is in a unity, and there is one God: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

last_rejected.quote: because the only Son is only from only, and the Holy Spirit is only

English 'the Holy Spirit is only' loses the grammatical gender distinction that emphasizes uniqueness of each person. Brief explicitly states: 'the grammar emphasizes the uniqueness of each person in the Trinity rather than procession "from" the Father alone.' last_rejected.ruling: 'is only' renders μόνον adequately; gender distinction is grammatical, not semantic loss. Within range.

problems.why: Same person rendered two ways; 'bar' explained in section 1 but not in intro.
problems.fix: Use one form consistently or gloss 'bar' at first occurrence.

problems.why: Intro lists 'only Son' as key term but uses 'Only-Begotten' as variant; section 1 uses 'only Son' for same Greek term.
problems.fix: Standardize to one English term throughout.

problems.quote: that they might have life in themselves
problems.why: Words attributed to Jesus but presented as indirect speech; reader may miss this is John 17:3 quotation.
problems.fix: Format as direct quotation or add 'as he said'.

problems.why: Incomplete sentence; 'only' seems to mean 'only Spirit' or 'from only,' but as printed suggests 'merely' or is ungrammatical.
problems.fix: Supply 'from only' or 'only Spirit' to match Trinitarian argument.

problems.quote: when he said: that they might have life in themselves, to know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent
problems.why: The colon after 'said' makes the following clause read as direct speech, but it is a paraphrase of John 17:3, not a quotation.
problems.fix: Replace colon with 'that': 'when he said that they might have life in themselves, to know...'

problems.why: The same Greek term monogenēs is rendered 'only Son' in the text but 'Only-Begotten' in the intro, potentially confusing readers.
problems.fix: Use one rendering consistently; note they are the same term.

problems.quote: the only Son is only from only, and the Holy Spirit is only
problems.why: The repetition of 'only' is opaque in English; the argument needs 'only-begotten from only-begotten' or 'unique from unique'.
problems.fix: Render as 'the only Son is from the only Father, and the Holy Spirit is only' or rephrase for clarity.

fixed: The 'Simon son of Jonah' issue is not a real problem in the English text: the English already renders the name consistently as 'Simon son of Jonah' and explains 'bar' as 'son' in the same sentence.

The 'only Son' glossary issue is not a real problem in the English text: the English consistently uses 'only Son' for the Greek term, and the work brief's glossary entry for Μονογενὴς lists 'only Son' as the decided English rendering.

The speaker attribution issue is not a real problem: the English already presents the John 17:3 material as indirect speech introduced by 'when he said', which is appropriate for the source's indirect construction.
The 'Holy Spirit is only' issue is addressed by supplying 'the only Father' in the preceding clause, which clarifies the Trinitarian argument without changing the source's emphasis on uniqueness.
The colon after 'said' is corrected to 'that' to match the source's indirect speech.
The repetition of 'only' is clarified by rendering 'only from only' as 'only from the only Father', preserving the source's emphasis on uniqueness while making the English grammatical and clear.
